div.head: Ger 15.1
div.ab: ⁊ fela towtola: flexlinan, spinle, reol, gearnwindan, stodlan, lorgas, presse, pihten, timplean, wifte, wefle, wulcamb, cip, amb, crancstæf, sceaðele, seamsticcan, scearra, nædle, slic.
7 fela towtola. flexlinan. Spinle . reol. gearnwindan . stodlan . lorgas. presse. pihten. timplean. wifte. wefle. wulcamb. cip amb. Crancstæf . Sceaðele. SeamSticcan .Scearra. Nædle . Slic.
And fela towtola: flexlinan, spinle, reol, gearnwindan, stodlan, lorgas, presse, pihten, timplean, wifte, wefle,ulcamb, cip, amb, crancstæf, sceaðele, seamsticcan, scearra, w nædle, slic.

und viele Spinngeräthe: Flachsleine, Spindel, Haspel, Garnwinde, Rietkamm des Webstuhls, Zeugbäume, [Tuch]presse, Weberkamm, Karden..?, Einschlag, Kette [oder Schiffchen], Wollkamm, Webebaum, Webespule [oder Riedblatt], Haspelstock, Schiffchen [?], ‘Saumstöcke’, kleine Scheere, Nadel, Schlägel.

and many spinning implements: flax-line, spindle, reel, yarn-winder, stodles [loom uprights], beams, press, comb, carders(?), weft, warp [or shuttle], wool-comb, loom-roller, slay [or reed], winding-stick, shuttle[?], seam-sticks, small shears, needle, beater.

and many spinning implements, a cord for hanging flax from, spindle, reel, yarn winder, weaver’s slay, distaff, clothes’ press, loom parts, [weavers’ instrument], [weavers’ instrument], [weavers’ instrument], wool comb, weaver’s beam, pail, [weaver’s instrument], shuttle, harness, [weaver’s instrument], shears, needle, mallet.

Also many spinning tools: a line for hanging flax, spindle, reel, yarn winders, loom uprights, heddle rods, a cloth press, comb beater, temples, weft thread, warp thread, wool comb, yoke beam, beater, crank, sheath, seam picks, fabric shears, needle, wooden mallet.
div.note: 1. B's ‘næfebor’ stands so. Liebermann's translations of the rarer terms are marked with queries; the English follows his German.; AZ: corrected against Rabin p. 336 / 337, October 2026 (was “[15.1]”, now “∅”)

spinning tools: The implements listed here have occasioned considerable critical head-scratching. Though some are recognizable tools still in use, others remain obscure. The confusion is exacerbated by the fact that many of the terms in this list occur nowhere else in Old English.

note.seg: S. Gl Weberei, die vor 1066 nur häuslich war; Cunningham 179⁵.—‘Werkzeug’ Kluge zu weit; s. Composita towcræft, -hus, -lic, -myderce
See Gl Weberei, which before 1066 was purely domestic; Cunningham 179⁵.—‘tool’ Kluge too wide; see the compounds towcræft, -hus, -lic, -myderce
‘Seil’ Kluge; spirae glossiert line (Ælfric); ‘reel’ Sweet; allein dies ist das hier folgende reol; ‘Flachswinde’ Sk-Wi
‘rope’ Kluge; line glosses spirae (Ælfric); ‘reel’ Sweet; but that is the reol that follows here; ‘flax-reel’ Sk-Wi
Mätzner 335
Mätzner 335
Mittelengl. telarium, lame de tisserant glossiert, jetzt studdles; ‘slay’ Toller, Sweet; unerklärt Sk
In Middle English it glosses telarium, lame de tisserant, now studdles; ‘slay’ Toller, Sweet; unexplained Sk
Glossiert colus, webbeam, liciatorium (Ælfric); ‘weaver's beam’ Toller, Sweet; ‘Spindel’ Kluge
Glosses colus, webbeam, liciatorium (Ælfric); ‘weaver's beam’ Toller, Sweet; ‘spindle’ Kluge
Mittelengl. pannicipium, vestiplicium glossiert
In Middle English it glosses pannicipium, vestiplicium
pecten glossiert
Glosses pecten
Nach Ritter (o. 12³) dt. tempel ‘Sperrute, Spannstock, Breithalter’
According to Ritter (above 12³) German tempel ‘spreading rod, stretcher, temple’
‘weft’ Sweet, Toller; fehlt Sk
‘weft’ Sweet, Toller; not in Sk
= ‘Aufzug’ (Kluge), ‘warp’ (Sweet); ‘weft’ Toller, wie md. wefel, wevel ‘Einschlag’ [so Sk-Wi] heisst. Aber es glossiert panniculae, d. i. panuclium ‘Weberschiffchen’. ‘Aufwinder’ Sk-Wi
= ‘warp’ (Kluge), ‘warp’ (Sweet); ‘weft’ Toller, as Middle German wefel, wevel means ‘weft’ [so Sk-Wi]. But it glosses panniculae, i.e. panuclium ‘weaver's shuttle’. ‘winder’ Sk-Wi

‘Webespule’ Kluge; ‘reed (Sweet) or slay’ [so Sk-Wi] Bo-Toller; Toller Suppl. identifiziert es mit dem cautere [Brenneisen] glossierenden Worte: das passt nicht. Camb emendiert Brasch Werkzeuge 59, m. E. unnötig, wenn auch das Vorkommen von camb hinter 17¹⁸ keinen Gegengrund bietet

‘weaving-bobbin’ Kluge; ‘reed (Sweet) or slay’ [so Sk-Wi] Bo-Toller; Toller Suppl. identifies it with the word glossing cautere [branding-iron]: that does not fit. Brasch Werkzeuge 59 emends to Camb, in my opinion unnecessarily, even though the occurrence of camb after 17¹⁸ offers no argument against it
‘Webstock?’ Kluge; crank noch jetzt; ‘Weife, Haspel, Kurbel, reel for winding thread’ Mätzner, Stratmann, Halliwell; ‘Wickler mit gebogenem Griff’ Sk-Wi
‘weaving-stick?’ Kluge; crank still today; ‘reel, windlass, crank, reel for winding thread’ Mätzner, Stratmann, Halliwell; ‘winder with a curved handle’ Sk-Wi
Nach Ritter (o. 12³) anord. skeið; ‘slay or weaver's rod’; ‘skuttle?’ Toller, ‘Weberschiff’ Sk-Wi; dies lautet mengl. scitil, schitel; Stratmann, Skeat
According to Ritter (above 12³) ON skeið; ‘slay or weaver's rod’; ‘skuttle?’ Toller, ‘weaver's shuttle’ Sk-Wi; in ME this is scitil, schitel; Stratmann, Skeat
Ich übersetze nur silbenhaft.—‘Nahthalter’ Sk-Wi
I translate only syllable by syllable.—‘seam-holder’ Sk-Wi
‘Hammer’ Kluge; ‘sleekstone’ [Glättstein; Sk-Wi] fürs Tuch Sweet, Toller; vgl. Bateson Records of Leicester I 71
‘hammer’ Kluge; ‘sleekstone’ [smoothing-stone; Sk-Wi] for the cloth Sweet, Toller; cf. Bateson Records of Leicester I 71
